hook: $27 of hardware is why this paint job looks finished

scenes.visual_prompt: Cabinet door off its hinges resting on a sawhorse, old brass pull still attached
scenes.voiceover: Every door's already off the hinges for the paint cure.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hand unscrewing an old brass pull from a cabinet door
scenes.voiceover: Which means this is the one window to swap hardware for free.

scenes.visual_prompt: 30-pack of matte black 5-inch pulls laid out on a counter, box shown
scenes.voiceover: A 30-pack of matte black pulls runs $26.99 — enough for a full kitchen in one order.

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up measuring screw spacing on an old pull against a new pull template
scenes.voiceover: Standard spacing means the new pulls usually line up with existing pilot holes — no redrilling.

scenes.visual_prompt: Drill driving in a new matte black pull on a freshly painted burnt-orange door
scenes.voiceover: It adds about an hour to a project that's already in progress.

scenes.visual_prompt: Finished burnt-orange cabinet door with matte black pull, reveal lighting
scenes.on_screen_text: Reads like a renovation, not a paint job
scenes.voiceover: That's the difference between 'cabinets someone painted' and a finished kitchen.

caption: Matte black hardware is the detail that makes a repainted cabinet look like an actual renovation instead of a weekend paint job. Doors are already off the hinges for cure time, so this is a one-hour add, not a second project. The pulls I'd order (38,159 ratings, 4.7 stars) are linked in the full post.
